item.dc:creator: George Kary
item.content:encoded:
BURNOUT’s posts on Substack now include a “listen to the post” feature with George Kary. This is in par with the project’s focus on up-skilling; the addition of audio offers the opportunity to practice audio mixing and American english. At some point, summary videos will also be introduced, to close the loop of embracing audiovisual formats.

Follow the experiment.

Subscribe now

The necessity for tackling audio design arose from a re-shuffle in the team - as we had to both recall quite a bit of material and reconsider the project’s production pipeline for its audiovisual components.

However, a side benefit of this extra challenge seems to be leading to an even higher quality in sound design, especially for the story’s mood setting videos.

So, please bare with us as we learn yet another discipline.

In terms of placement on the Substack posts, after a little bit of experimentation, we decided to place the audio snippets beneath the posts’s cover. The goal is to immerse readers with the visual parts first - that’s the cover and at a later stage, the summary video with George Kary - then, right before the drop cap initiating the text portion of the post, comes the audio snippet.

Readers can just click to listen, instead of, well, reading. Ah…

For the curious, the drop cap is the capitalised letter at the beginning of text. In our case, we intentionally always start posts with the word “BURNOUT”.

At least for the meta-story; the story’s chapters, of course, vary.

We’ll be updating posts from the past as we go along.

Finally, we also updated all the covers and cover templates for posts; the BURNOUT logo was taking too much real estate on the creatives.

After all, burnout is another one of the story’s misdirections.

item.title: 4 project phases, 1 intent
item.description: BURNOUT is an experimental, multi-disciplinary project focused on upskilling, with 4 phases.
item.dc:creator: George Kary
item.content:encoded:
BURNOUT is an experimental, multi-disciplinary project focused on upskilling, with 4 phases: setting the stage, the build-up, the release of the story and a retrospective BTS-focused part. We’re currently approaching the end of the first phase and entering the build-up stage, which means the focus will now start to shift to the multimedia aspect.

So, let’s take a look at the agenda.

Follow the experiment.

Subscribe now

Owing to the story’s own modular architecture relying on the three major acts of storytelling, the project’s phases, are, well, acts themselves; aiming to make audiences feel that distinct act-change effect on the project level, as well.

But more on that, later. Back to the phases.

Act 1: Setting the stage.

This phase was necessary for various reasons, however, the core premise was to turn a largely unorganised attempt that started in August of 2025 (a year ago) into a coherent ecosystem with a meta-narrative for creating the narrative itself.

Simply put, we had no idea what we were doing for months, despite the lingering presence of an architecture that had not taken shape, yet.

  1. Author’s Notes

    1. Introduction (published)

    2. An AI-augmented creative project (published)

    3. Characters and character progression (published)

    4. The process of experimentation (published)

    5. 4 project phases, 1 intent (current)

    6. The project is a meta-story itself

    7. A story that’s actually built on a plot-twist

    8. Release formats and mediums

    9. Locations in Greece, Malta and Italy

    10. Social media metrics and insights

  2. Github, now available (published)

  3. Prologue, now available

  4. Blackscript, now available ~ a storytelling skill for AI agents (incl. Custom GPT) with pacing, structuring, hooks and proofreading workflows

  5. Audio, now available

The final item on the agenda will introduce audio versions on each post on Substack, completing the phase. This particular feature also presents a much needed opportunity to upskill in audio mixing (sound design has been honed in for months alongside videography) and speech with American english.

A new Gallery may pop-up with the series’s artwork (alternatively, the knowledge base on Github will be used for context ingestion).

Act 2: Build-up.

At this second phase, the narrative will shift its focus back from the project to the story and the elements of the story. Since this is, after all, an endeavour in multimedia, and not just written form, a new parallel thread will also begin.

  1. Substack will continue where it left of.

  2. Tiktok - the series’s main outlet for short-form and George Kary’s own Instagram and YouTube will introduce Author’s Notes videos that pick up from the beginning (setting the stage).

Let’s take a look at the build-up’s upcoming content:

  1. Author’s Notes

    1. Meet the Id

    2. Meet the Ego

    3. Meet the Superego

    4. Freud’s battlefield as a dramatic driver

    5. Sequence and symbolism of the logo

    6. Mood setting videos and series theme

  2. Video, now available

Just like audio for the first stage, the final item for this second stage will introduce “In a Nutshell” videos to all Substack posts, thus closing the preparation loop with short-form videos on TikTok, IG and YT.

YouTube will feature the following playlists:

  1. In a Nutshell ~ focused on the meta-story.

  2. Set the Mood (YT Shorts) ~ focused on the story itself.

  3. OSTs ~ of the music used in the series’s mood setting short-form videos.

Act 3: Release of the story.

Audiences will have the following options to consume the story:

  1. Purchase a digital copy of the entire book (i.e. Amazon).

  2. Follow Substack’s pace and read chapter-by-chapter ~ chapters will be made available only for paid members after 48 hours of a chapter’s free release.

Prior to the launch (both one-off for the book and phased on Substack):

  1. Sequence of teasers from the prologue

  2. Trailer, now available

  3. Author’s Note

    1. Sequence of teasers and the trailer

3 parts with 19 chapters in total, with each following:

  1. A mood setting short-form video

  2. An author’s note dissecting it with a nutshell video

Retrospective.

The final phase is focused on the BTS (Behind the Scenes).

  1. Epilogue, now available

  2. Author’s Note

    1. Hidden meaning of the cover and the plot-twist

    2. Takeaways from the experiment

  3. BTS

    1. Pixar’s 3-layer narrative

    2. Campbell’s monomyth

    3. Snyder’s logline

    4. Nolan’s non-linear timelines

    5. Acts, phases, beats and buts

    6. Narrative devices and techniques

    7. Glitches, layers of clothes and travel footage

    8. Storyline, architecture and scripting

    9. Lighting and composition
      ft. (Instagram)

    10. Videography, sound design and audio mixing
      ft.

  4. Materials & Guides

    1. Storytelling crash-course with Blackaft

    2. Lighting and composition

    3. Sound design and audio mixing with Garageband for MacOS

    4. Video editing with Capcut

    5. Creative (product) design with Canva

    6. Drone shots with DJI’s Neo

    7. Travel information

The series’s GPT will continuously be extended with the project’s knowledge base on Github, alongside newly published posts on Substack.

So, that was the 4 phases of the Burnout Series project.

item.title: Github, now available
item.description: BURNOUT embraces AI strictly for analysis, distribution in some parts and post-consumption, not consumption.
item.dc:creator: George Kary
item.content:encoded:
BURNOUT embraces AI strictly for analysis, distribution in some parts and post-consumption, not consumption. Put your ass down and read, like humans used to before 2023. That means, the series does not use AI to generate any kind of content for the series itself, including scripts, multimedia and posts on Substack. Those are made by humans, for humans. But, in this day and age, using AI to interact with any kind of material absolutely makes sense.

So, let’s distribute context for AI next to content for humans.

Follow the experiment.

Subscribe now

The new repository is agnostic, in terms of AI setups. While it’s currently working for the series’s Custom GPT in strictly production terms, the repository was tested with isolated ChatGPT sessions, Codex, Claude and a BYOK setup including VS Code + Cline for the agentic management.

That means, if you don’t prefer GPT, you can use the repository’s manifest - and even the repository itself by forking it - to set up your own stream for the series.

It’s essentially a workflow, with a very rudimentary advent of RAG principles.

This is, of course, in alignment with Blackaft’s principle of distributing content from and to AI, acknowledging that humans use AI to consume, anyway.

Feel free to fork the repo on Github and experiment yourself.

Whereas the workflow so far for the series’s custom GPT included manually updating relevant files on the GPT, the new workflow is programmatic.

Now, the process is much more simple:

  1. Humans publish on Substack and append the updated RSS feed, including any additional images or contextual changes to the repository

  2. Humans or their AIs can run a robust publishing script

  3. All done - Custom GPT and all AIs hooking to the series’s stream have the new context, using Github’s own raw content service

Why is the first step still manual?

We ran into firewall issues with Substack, since their images are served via CDN to avoid violent scrapes, and the RSS is, we gathered, blocked programmatically.

A natural solution to that would be to use Apify’s built-in Substack scrapers.

But hey, we ain’t gonna pay that much for a measly experiment!

item.title: Materials & Guides: Explore your thoughts with the series's preloaded ChatGPT
item.description: Being an experiment, the Burnout Series embraces AI as a natural part of the analysis process, both before and after distributing and consuming content.
item.dc:creator: George Kary
item.content:encoded:
BURNOUT is a series that intentionally embraces the complexity of multi-thread narration, both in the story and the meta. Both represent inexplicable pieces of the project’s own deconstruction-in-construction process, since the project itself is the actual meta-storyline.

But that wouldn’t really work without AI, these days, would it?

You’d immediately lose your audience.

Follow the experiment.

So, it was of paramount importance to embrace the fact that audiences absolutely use AI these days to dive and understand. However, using AI to research and analyse the material that’s published, in a silo, is just one side of the coin.

The other side is letting audiences tap into your project’s knowledge base.

So, we released a custom GPT to help audiences explore their thoughts on posts - both story and meta.

But, it’s got no spoilers or hints, don’t get too excited.

How it works.

Every time a new post springs up on Substack, the custom GPT’s knowledge base is extended with the new post - and any complementary, vibe-setting, photos or additional context awareness instructions and data.

You’ll find the link at the bottom of posts and on the menu.

Click it, and off you go.

You’ll need at least a free account with ChatGPT to use it.

How to make your own.

You’ll need a paid account with ChatGPT to create one.

Head over to chatgpt.com and make sure you’re signed in with your desired account at the bottom left.

Go to settings and navigate to:

  1. Billing ~ verify your desired public name

  2. Account ~ quickly setup your GPT builder profile, which allows you to optionally connect and publicly display your LinkedIn / GitHub profiles

Back to the left panel, (more), GPTs, and on the top right corner, hit “Create”.

item.title: Process of experimentation
item.description: BURNOUT is an experimental series - the process of making it is equally - if not more - important as the actual story itself.
item.dc:creator: George Kary
item.content:encoded:
BURNOUT is an experimental series - the process of making it is equally - if not more - important as the actual story itself. After all, it is an exercise in upskilling on various fields and an effort born out of a passion for tackling multi-disciplinary and cross-functional projects (continues).

But let’s get back to the process.

Follow the experiment.

The Story

Deconstructing a seemingly superficial story of travel and injecting a little bit of drama into it (103 days of backpacking across 3 countries) still kept the surface level at the center of the narrative.

It had no grit. No backbone.

That’s where the concept of burnout came in: the emotional layer beneath all this fancy scenery and drone shots. It marked the beginning of a conflict.

And there’s really no good story without a conflict.

But that wasn’t enough. Feeling restless after years of not taking a vacation? Big deal. Undoing your life and embracing solo travel? There’s no resonance for viewers and readers alike - hell, there’s no resonance for the creator, either.

So, the more analytical the deconstruction of the story became - and the more testing on social media affirmed these assumptions of “bleh”, the more organic it felt that there was a deeper layer, the core layer.

Freud’s civil war (cited) - the bullshit we tell ourselves.

Now that, will absolutely resonate. And it did in closed testing.

But in order for it to work, the narrative needs to completely embrace absurdity, maintain an anti-mainstream attitude across the entire story and point the middle finger to the superficial beauty of social media.

It’s gotta make you uncomfortable, because the conflict is internal.

Upcoming BTS (Behind the Scenes) and Author’s Notes on the story:

~ BTS ~
Pixar’s 3-layer narrative
Campbell’s monomyth
Snyder’s logline
Nolan’s non-linear timelines
Acts and phases
Beats and buts
Devices and narrative techniques
Scripting and episodic format
Long-form vs short-form

~ Author's Notes ~
Locations (Malta, Italy, Greece)

The Characters

To offset the bluntness of the “travel documentary” effect, we needed to satisfy one more condition for effective storytelling.

We needed a hero for the conflict.

Or an anti-hero (ref).

This was easy - having Freud’s work laid out in front of us, deciding on the 3 main characters was instant: the Id, the Ego and the Superego. What we had to figure out was the binding thread between them.

Sure, they’re arguing.

But why?

We had to connect the story’s concept of burnout with that internal misalignment we all feel at various parts in our lives. How the id craves pleasure and comfort; how the superego stands judgemental; and how the ego rationalises.

Now that last part - the rationalisation - began to resonate with the conflict and the story’s veil of absurdity.

You can tell who’s the asshole easily.

But there’s still something wrong, as we employ various narrative devices at most, if not all, unexpected places, setting the stage for the conflict’s climax and the ensuing plot-twist resolution at the end.

A good story leaves an after-taste; one that resonates personally.

So, we had the journey - and we had the hero.

It was time to get back to the technical aspects, for without them, even a good story with good characters can suck.

Upcoming BTS (Behind the Scenes) and Author’s Notes on the characters:

~ BTS ~ 
Constructing the Id, Ego and Superego characters
Glitches and clothes as narrative devices
Travel & drone footage
Series’s non-linear storyline

~ Author’s Notes ~ 
Meet the Id, Ego and Superego characters
Freud’s battlefield
Symbolism and sequence of the logo

The Mechanics

First of all, simply to conclude the conjunction (and juxtaposition) of the story with the characters clashing, it just made good sense to put a simplifying label on the whole thing - and thus, the 3 parts were born:

  1. Dissonance ~ set in Italy, backwards

  2. Resonance ~ set in Greece, forwards

  3. Convergence ~ set again in Greece, but backwards (the last chapter is whimsically called Origins of Delusion)

Then we had to figure out lighting, composition, photography and videography from scratch (video editing is relatively easy to learn, in comparison). It was important to capture a similar Christopher Nolan vibe across all POVs, including Author’s Notes and BTS (inspired by Tenet’s (cited) palette).

That’s new media and cinematic for you. The story itself feels like you’re in someone’s head, hence the intense colors, dead pans and center placed characters. The Ego is, well, a Netflix-styled interview, but, absurd.

Then came theming, sound design and audio mixing. Nothing fancy, but the goal was to make something that’d be worth going back to years from now.

And finally, formats and channels for publishing the series (and the book).

It’s all pretty straightforward.

Upcoming BTS (Behind the Scenes) and Author’s Notes on the mechanics:

Lighting (ft. Thanos Doumas)
Composition
Color balancing and grading

item.title: Characters and character progression
item.description: BURNOUT’s primary character is the Ego, played by George Kary. The story begins with the Ego being absurdly obnoxious, arrogant, superior and patronising (sometimes breaking the fourth wall for dramatic effect), looking back and remembering a 103-day backpacking trip, feasting on its victory over burnout and its accomplishments. As the story unfolds, its assumptions and certainty appear and feel hollow. The Ego begins to unravel and spiral, ultimately forced to face the secondary characters at the end of the series.
item.dc:creator: George Kary
item.content:encoded:
BURNOUT’s primary character is the Ego, played by George Kary. The story begins with the Ego being absurdly obnoxious, arrogant, superior and patronising (sometimes breaking the fourth wall for dramatic effect), looking back and remembering a 103-day backpacking trip, feasting on its victory over burnout and its accomplishments. As the story unfolds, its assumptions and certainty appear and feel hollow. The Ego begins to unravel and spiral, ultimately forced to face the secondary characters at the end of the series.

Follow the experiment.

The secondary characters are the Id and the Superego, loosely inspired by Freud’s fundamental principles on human identity. They are silent, interfering with the Ego’s delusions, as both of them have been excluded from the Ego’s understanding of the self. As the story unfolds, both attempt to drive their separate agendas against each other, taking hits, until they are also forced to face the primary character for the final realization (plot twist reveal).

The Ego is the only narrator both in the teaser videos and the text chapters, rambling incessantly and driving the story forward (MacGuffin device, also paired with the Unreliable Narrator narrative device).

Secondary characters.

  • The Id represents the raw, sensual, primal side of the self, seeking pleasure, comfort and the “good old days”. It represents the past. The narrative intentionally paints the Id as the victim of the entire series. It’s a Red Herring narrative device (misdirection).

    ~ rim chroma = blue

  • The Superego represents the judgemental figure and moral compass, relentlessly pushing forward, offering no room or rest. It represents the future. It’s also a Foreshadowing device meant to offset the Red Herring Id and the Unreliable Narrator Ego, as it looks clearly menacing and the “bad guy” in the story.

    ~ rim chroma = red, opposite light/dark sides to the Id for lighting

Emotional states.

Both secondary characters undergo 6 different emotional states (+1 exclusively reserved for the ending sequence and the plot twist reveal).

  1. Part One: Dissonance ~ represents Act 1 of the entire series

    1. Exposition ~ an obnoxious and analytical Ego with a determined Superego and a playful Id (both dark T-Shirt)

    2. Inciting Incident ~ Ego turns aggressive, both Superego and Id become uncertain and in disbelief (dark undershirt)

  2. Part Two: Resonance ~ Act 2 of the entire series

    1. Rising Action ~ Ego is now troubled and while both are concerned, the Superego is plotting and the Id appears deep in thought (grey T-Shirt)

    2. Midpoint ~ Ego replaces its analytical mode with an emotional stance going defensive, the Superego looks cunning and the Id annoyed (grey undershirt)

  3. Part Three: Convergence ~ Act 3

    1. Pre-Climax ~ determined Ego, victimised Superego, furious Id (white T-Shirt)

    2. Climax ~ controlling, furious and victimised (white undershirt).

    3. Resolution ~ no spoilers (duh)

Technical aspects.

Both secondary characters wear a beanie across all states.

All photo and video material used across all methods and channels showcase both characters above the chest with the collarbone and just enough of the shoulders-to-forearms ratio to achieve the “part of one” symbolism.

The colors, layers of clothes and glitching and trilateral sequence appearances of both secondary characters represent a Chekhov’s Gun narrative device (vital clues for introducing, expanding and revealing upon the core identity layer).

item.title: An AI-augmented creative project
item.description: BURNOUT is a purely creative project, with text, images and videos exclusively created by humans, for humans, in alignment with Blackaft’s principles, the biztech venture firm founded by George Kary. But the project has long been augmented by AI chatbots; at first, it was ChatGPT and then it became Gemini. That is, to say, augmentation strictly focused on research, context building, transposing data and, of course, refining iterations through a post-mortem process of analysing human-made content and metrics.
item.dc:creator: George Kary
item.content:encoded:
BURNOUT is a purely creative project, with text, images and videos exclusively created by humans, for humans, in alignment with Blackaft’s principles, the biztech venture firm founded by George Kary. But the project has long been augmented by AI chatbots; at first, it was ChatGPT and then it became Gemini. That is, to say, augmentation strictly focused on research, context building, transposing data and, of course, refining iterations through a post-mortem process of analysing human-made content and metrics.

This is all just a fancy way to say humans make stuff by using AI before and after the humans-making-stuff process takes place.

Follow the experiment.

Balancing both sides of the aisle has been a massive hurdle, especially in terms of record keeping. You know how it goes: you open a conversation on ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, etc., only to have the damn thing locked in that particular session, essentially unavailable to all other chats.

Naturally tackling launches, pivots and AI adoption, Blackaft employed an AI-augmentation-first approach from the start.

It also meant that launches, pivots and especially AI adoption may and will require human creativity, which is essentially what this series gradually became across the many months that George Kary has been going at it.

A practice run.

Blackaft Studio.

BURNOUT now lives under https://github.com/blackaft, with a little bit of Google Drive and Google Photos for handling multimedia.

For the devs/biztech folk out there, the setup - and Blackaft’s philosophy - is generally agnostic in terms of the tool or model, as a core foundational premise to be able to serve clients by embedding into their own operations to more effectively tackle launches and pivots. Since the repository also adheres to the firm’s central infrastructure direction, the cost to initialise such a thing with a VS Code + Cline + BYOK via Google’s Agent Platform setup was a meagre $0.98.

Mind you, the agent was on auto-pilot. It just received a single command, and 3-4 additional prompts that were specific to the Burnout Series.

The process is also self-improving; meaning there are deterministic workflows inherent to the agentic setup focused on iterating minor improvements the more data the repository builds (i.e. knowledge bases or LLM Vaults).

Suffice to say, Gemini remains the king across benchmarking in terms of handling context for such type of processes in building up blocks on top of blocks.

Results.

Why does this entire thing matter? Sure, it sounds fancy; a creative project using such a “coding” level of AI?

Outside helping with the actual production content and schedule, this post was crafted by a human in less than 10 minutes. The thoughts and raw notes were already there since September 2025. The AI, operating inside that Blackaft Studio agentic setup, was able to provide the human with all the necessary context.

And also, every post now has a prompt. Made by machines, for machines. This is, after all, all about embracing the world’s impending duality of the extremes.

Machines on the back; humans at the front.

item.title: Introduction
item.description: He backpacked to fix burnout. But burnout was just a battlefield. To heal, he must end the war.
item.dc:creator: George Kary
item.content:encoded:
BURNOUT is an experimental series created by George Kary, born out of a passion for tackling multi-disciplinary and cross-functional projects. The purpose of the series is to explore:

  1. Cinematography and storytelling. Techniques and principles, writing itself, lighting, editing, photography - you name it.

  2. Long-form content and short-form format. Also fiddling with the rising trends of micro-learning and micro-drama.

  3. Philosophical exercise in multimedia mode. Essentially exploring Freud’s concept of the Ego, Id and Superego and the idea that internal misalignment is what actually causes the thing we call “burnout”.

Follow the experiment.

The entire attempt, spanning from September 2025 to summer of 2026, led to leveraging all these learnings into a professional offering, as part of the human-heavy element of handling launches, pivots and AI adoption.

George is the founder of Blackaft Associates which offers a centralised management and delivery collective of biztech experts for startups and SMEs.

Across that period, multiple rounds of tests and iterations took place, including post-mortem analysis of social media metrics.

AI was heavily leveraged for augmenting research, testing and compiling a unified context for production. No content was generated by AI, in alignment with the human-for-humans principle.

So, all the theory and practice that went into creating, testing and finally launching the series, was, in essence, about rapid up-skilling.

Story.

The story is based on George’s own 3-month backpacking trip across Greece and Italy, back in 2025, when he decided to double-down on his new direction.

It’s, of course, over-dramatised to help achieve his exploration goals.

The Ego reminisces about the trip, as proof that it fixed burnout, once again taking charge of what was, up to that point, a fractured identity.

However, the Id and the Superego remain misaligned with the Ego’s self-rationalisations. As the Ego peels layer after layer to prove its victory, the full-fledged civil war surfaces between the 3 sides; an inner turmoil that no amount of analysis, travel or even emotional retrospection can resolve.

Except the tool of self-realisation, which everybody avoids out of shame and insecurity when it comes to confronting the reality of their selves, choices and environments, and not their dressed up versions.

The story takes place across 104 days, mostly in reverse chronological order. This particular choice of narrative format helps express the unravelling of the false assumptions that we all hold based on a preferential and skewed view of our memories; or rather, how we choose to interpret those memories.

Thus, the narrative was created in such a way to intentionally expose the entire story’s layers, one by one:

  1. The travel layer - oh, a guy who went backpacking to feel good

  2. The emotional layer - oh, he felt really bad

  3. The identity layer - oh, he was lying to himself all along

In summary, the series hopes to help viewers resonate with their own truths (and layers) by presenting the entire story with such raw brutality that it contrasts heavily with the content presented online and especially on social media.

Making it so uncomfortable and infuriating to watch someone being so publicly absurd that it triggers cognitive dissonance with your own private absurdity.

And making you not being able to stop watching to fill the gap.

Structure.

3 parts, 19 chapters total. Each chapter is complemented with a short-form video, meant to help set the mood for viewers.

Then you read the chapter.

That’s it.
